transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO Copperwind), Maya (ENG Lead), Jonas (Security), Priya DS

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Copperwind's path from prototype to first production inference. Main tension: use hosted Redwood API for fastest time-to-first-token vs Dedicated/Private for data residency and audit requirements. Customer wants a hands-on quickstart (PLG) but has enterprise constraints around logs and keymgmt.

Topics discussed:
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) with free credits and sandbox
- Data residency / VPC vs hosted API tradeoffs
- Latency vs cost and batching strategies
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2 questions
- Pilot sizing (QPS, token volumes) and success criteria

Action items (recap at end): see metadata action_items above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we've got about 45 minutes — I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, with Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Alex (CTO): Good, thanks, we appreciate the time. Quick context — Copperwind builds analytics pipelines for retail partners and we've been experimenting with reranking and summarization models. Want to understand how fast we can get to a safe prod path.
[00:19] Priya (SE): Great, quick note on agenda — we usually cover TTFT with credits, then hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security checklist, and pilot sizing. Feel free to interrupt.
[00:31] Maya (Eng Lead): Sounds good. Our main hard requirement is no raw PII leaving VPC for the first 3 months, after that we'll evaluate. So interested in what Hosted can offer vs VPC private deployment.
[00:42] Samir: Totally — that's common. For TTFT you can spin up the hosted Redwood API with self-serve credits we provide. Typically teams are able to make their first call within couple hours, sometimes minutes if they've got API keys. We'll send sandbox tokens.
[00:56] Alex: Couple questions — how are logs handled in hosted? We need audit logs but can't have debug-level payloads stored longer than 30 days.
[01:07] Priya: On hosted we have retention controls and can disable full payload retention; audit logs are available and we can integrate with customer SIEM for events. For strict residency, Redwood Private (VPC) is the option — private control-plane and you keep the data in your VPC.
[01:24] Jonas (Security): When you say integrate with SIEM, is it push or pull? We run Splunk and need S3 exports for compliance.
[01:33] Priya: We support S3 export, and we can push to your Splunk via a connector. Also support KMS key wrapping if you want to manage keys. There's an extra enterprise opt.
[01:43] Alex: Ok. So for a quickstart pilot can we use hosted but with masked payload retention?
[01:49] Samir: Yes. Many customers do a hosted pilot with retention off and then move to VPC/Dedicated after they validate. It's faster and lower friction.
[01:58] Maya: What's the pricing model for credits and what do credits cover?
[02:02] Samir: We issue free sandbox credits for PLG onramp which cover token usage in the hosted sandbox. We'll send you a worksheet that maps credits to expected token volumes and estimated spend post credits.
[02:13] Priya: Also quick perf note — latency vs cost tradeoffs: if you care about p95 latency at low tokens, smaller sequence models with FP16 or int8 quantized variants help. We recommend batching config and KV cache enabled for chat-style workloads.
[02:29] Alex: Can we do a small benchmark — maybe 50 concurrent requests, avg 200 tokens per call to mimic reranking.
[02:36] Priya: Yes we can. If you share expected QPS and percentiles, we can run a sandbox perf and return a CSV. We'll include suggested batch sizes and which model variants to use.
[02:48] Maya: What's the cadence for rolling to dedicated? Suppose we like perf and want predictable throughput.
[02:53] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly commit. You can start on hosted, then when you hit predictability thresholds we help size a Dedicated pool. It includes autoscaling policies and SLA-backed latency targets. Migration is straightforward: same API, pin model versions.
[03:09] Alex: Sounds promising. On the security front our compliance team will ask about SOC2 and logging — do you have customers who've done full SOC2 review for Private?
[03:18] Priya: Yes; Private deployments are common for regulated customers. We provide audit logs, RBAC via SSO, KMS/HSM integrations, and we can run security reviews and share SOC2 documentation under NDA.
[03:30] Jonas: Also curious about model governance — if we use Redwood model catalog with open models, can we pin an internal variant or is retraining required?
[03:39] Samir: You can pin specific model versions. If you have a custom fine-tuned model we can host that too in Private/Dedicated. For hosted we have curated models and Redwood-verified performance profiles.
[03:50] Alex: Any gotchas re: kv cache and memory on longer contexts? Our reranking sometimes uses 8k context.
[03:57] Priya: Longer contexts increase memory; the runtime picks optimized kernels and memory patterns. We'll suggest quantization profiles and caching — prefix caching can save a lot of tokens. But if you need consistent p95 for 8k we might recommend Dedicated with larger GPUs.
[04:13] Maya: If we start with hosted pilot, what's realistic TTFT? You said hours but I want a plan.
[04:19] Samir: Plan: Day 0 - provide sandbox tokens and quickstart guide; Day 1 - customer's devs make first calls and run simple evals; Day 2-3 - we run a perf harness based on your QPS and report back; Week 1 - iterate on config and discuss next steps (dedicated sizing or Private). That's typical for PLG-onramp.
[04:38] Alex: Great. On ownership of logs during pilot — is debug-level captured by default?
[04:43] Priya: Not by default; default is no full payload retention in sandbox. You can opt-in.
[04:48] Jonas: Encryption at rest? KMS?
[04:51] Priya: Yes, encryption at rest is standard. For Private we support customer-managed KMS keys/hsm, for hosted we use managed keys but can do envelope encryption.
[05:02] Unassigned Speaker 1: sorry quick interruption our SRE asked about DNS and egress — if we use Private in VPC what's the networking model?
[05:12] Priya: For Private we provide a customer-managed VPC peering or private endpoint depending on cloud. Egress is controlled; you can route outbound through your NATs, and we document ports and subnets.
[05:24] Alex: Let's talk numbers — what does 50 QPS / 200 tokens look like cost-wise in hosted?
[05:29] Samir: We'll send an estimate in the pricing worksheet, but rough sketch: with batching and kv caching you'd lower per-token cost. For that profile you might see X tokens/minute and we map credits. We'll provide concrete numbers after perf run.
[05:44] Maya: One more question — do you support function calling / structured outputs? Our annotators need JSON fields back reliably.
[05:51] Priya: Yes, hosted API supports structured outputs and function/tool calling. We'll point you to the sample prompts and parsing guide.
[05:59] Alex: Who typically is the SE point during the pilot?
[06:02] Samir: Priya will be the main SE; she'll own the perf checklist and help run the sandbox harness.
[06:08] Maya: Good. Regarding rollout policy — if we hit regression we want automatic fallback to a smaller model. Is that supported?
[06:15] Priya: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy — you can define priority and cost thresholds.
[06:24] Alex: Ok thanks. Any enterprise blockers we should anticipate?
[06:28] Samir: The typical blockers are KMS requirements, legal NDAs, and long-term data residency. Those are solvable — we usually do an initial hosted pilot under stricter retention then evaluate Private.
[06:40] Jonas: For legal I'll need a data processing addendum. Can you provide a template?
[06:44] Samir: Yes, we'll include the DPA and SOC2 docs in the packet.
[06:48] Maya: What's the SLA for Dedicated?
[06:51] Priya: Dedicated has monthly uptime targets and latency SLOs — we'll share the SLA doc.
[06:55] Alex: Ok let's lock next steps.
[06:58] Samir: Recap: we'll send quickstart guide + sandbox tokens and credits worksheet (Samir), Priya will share perf checklist and batching recommendations and run a perf harness after you share QPS, Alex to share expected QPS and retention policy. Schedule a deeper technical call next week.
[07:16] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone.
[07:18] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email.

(Notes: transcript ends earlier than wall clock as some sections summarized. Several small transcription mistakes present: 'keymgmt' transcribed as keymgmt and "KV cache" as "key-v cache" in some places.)
